authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws
authority.section: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(a), definition of collaborative drug therapy management

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Collaborative drug therapy management is the initiating, monitoring, modifying and discontinuing of a patient's drug therapy by a pharmacist in accordance with a collaborative practice agreement. It MAY include collecting and reviewing patient histories; obtaining and checking vital signs, including pulse, temperature, blood pressure and respiration; and, under the supervision of, or in direct consultation with, a physician, ordering and evaluating the results of laboratory tests directly related to drug therapy when performed in accordance with approved protocols applicable to the practice setting AND WHEN THE EVALUATION SHALL NOT INCLUDE A DIAGNOSTIC COMPONENT.

authority.name: Pharmacist qualifications for collaborative drug therapy management

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A collaborating pharmacist must satisfy Massachusetts licensure, experience or degree, liability insurance, practice-focus, and additional annual continuing-education requirements.
exceptions: Apply any narrower setting-specific, product-specific, or emergency exception before the general rule.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 16.02(1), in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(b), to qualify to enter into a collaborative practice agreement and engage in collaborative practice a pharmacist must: (a) hold a CURRENT UNRESTRICTED LICENSE IN GOOD STANDING to practice pharmacy in the Commonwealth and currently be engaged in pharmacy practice in the Commonwealth; (b) maintain at least $1,000,000 (PER OCCURRENCE) of professional liability insurance DURING THE TERM OF THE AGREEMENT WHICH SPECIFICALLY COVERS DRUG THERAPY MANAGEMENT; (c) have completed five years of experience as a licensed pharmacist OR have satisfied one of the requirements in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c)1. through 2., which are 1. have earned a doctor of pharmacy degree AND have entered into a collaborative practice agreement ON OR BEFORE JUNE 30, 2017, or 2. have completed such other education or residency criteria that the Board determines to be the equivalent of five years experience as a licensed pharmacist; (d) devote a portion of practice to the defined drug therapy area that the pharmacist shall co-manage; and (e) complete, in each year of the term of the agreement, at least five additional contact hours of Board-approved continuing education that address areas of practice generally related to THE PARTICULAR collaborative practice agreement. 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) states further conditions, at 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)1. through 3., if prescriptive practices are included in the agreement.
exceptions: 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c) is satisfied by five years of experience as a licensed pharmacist, or by 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c)1., a doctor of pharmacy degree together with a collaborative practice agreement entered on or before June 30, 2017, or by 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c)2., other education or residency criteria the Board determines to be the equivalent of five years experience.
247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) applies only if prescriptive practices are included in the collaborative practice agreement.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Medicine regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 243 CMR 2.12(2), in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(b), to qualify to enter into a collaborative practice agreement a pharmacist must: (a) hold a current unrestricted license in good standing to practice pharmacy in the Commonwealth and currently be engaged in pharmacy practice in the Commonwealth; (b) agree to maintain at least $1,000,000 (per occurrence) of professional liability insurance during the term of the agreement which specifically covers drug therapy management; (c) HAVE EARNED A DOCTOR OF PHARMACY DEGREE OR HAVE COMPLETED FIVE YEARS OF EXPERIENCE as a licensed pharmacist; (d) agree to devote a portion of the practice to the defined drug therapy area that the pharmacist shall co-manage; (e) agree to complete, in each year of the term of the agreement, at least five additional contact hours OR 0.5 CONTINUING EDUCATION UNITS of Board of Registration in Pharmacy approved continuing education that address areas of practice generally related to the particular collaborative practice agreement; and (f) if prescriptive practices are included in the agreement, agree to maintain a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department during the term of the agreement, pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Medicine regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 243 CMR 2.12(1), Authorized Pharmacist means a pharmacist who: (a) is currently registered by the Board of Registration in Pharmacy and is in good standing; (b) MEETS THE REQUIREMENTS OF 247 CMR 16.02: Pharmacist Qualifications; and (c) is participating in drug therapy management with a supervising physician pursuant to a written CDTM agreement with written protocols. The three limbs are stated together.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Collaborative drug therapy management is allowed in hospitals licensed under M.G.L. c. 111, s. 51, SUBJECT TO APPROVAL BY THE MEDICAL STAFF EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE or designee; long-term care facilities licensed under s. 71, subject to approval by the FACILITY'S MEDICAL DIRECTOR or designee; inpatient or outpatient hospice settings licensed under s. 57D, subject to approval by the HOSPICE'S MEDICAL DIRECTOR or designee; and ambulatory care clinics licensed under s. 51, WITH ON-SITE SUPERVISION by the attending physician and a collaborating pharmacist, subject to approval by the clinic's medical staff executive committee or designee, or medical director or designee.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws
Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A physician or physician group MAY hire pharmacists for the purpose of practising collaborative drug therapy management under an agreement for the benefit of a patient of that physician or group. NO retail pharmacy may employ a physician FOR THE PURPOSE of maintaining, establishing or entering into a collaborative practice agreement. Nothing prohibits a retail pharmacy from hiring a physician or licensed medical practitioner for the purpose of conducting QUALITY ASSURANCE REVIEWS of its pharmacists engaged in collaborative drug therapy management.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Medicine regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 243 CMR 2.12(3)(a), to be eligible to participate in a collaborative drug therapy management agreement a physician must possess an active license to practice medicine issued by the Board AND must be ACTIVELY ENGAGED IN THE CLINICAL PRACTICE of medicine and the provision of patient care IN THE PARTICULAR FIELD of medicine in which the collaborative drug therapy management is to take place. Under 243 CMR 2.12(3)(b) the physician is the supervisor in the agreement and RETAINS THE ULTIMATE RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE CARE OF THE PATIENT, and in a community pharmacy setting a physician should enter into only as many agreements as he or she can reasonably and safely supervise at one time. Under 243 CMR 2.12(3)(c) the supervising physician SHALL ASSESS THE PATIENT AND MAKE A WRITTEN REFERRAL of the identified patient to the authorized pharmacist, and that written referral shall include a primary diagnosis and any co-morbid conditions that are included in the collaborative drug therapy management.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Medicine regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A physician is INELIGIBLE to participate in collaborative drug therapy management if he or she is in a Voluntary Agreement Not to Practice Medicine with the Board, or has had a licence to practise medicine temporarily suspended or revoked. A physician SHALL BE DEEMED INELIGIBLE if he or she has VOLUNTARILY SURRENDERED or has had SUSPENDED, REVOKED OR RESTRICTED a controlled substances licence, permit or registration, EITHER STATE OR FEDERAL. Where the Board acts against a physician it MAY require the physician to notify each authorized pharmacist with whom the physician is in an agreement.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws
authority.section: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(a), definition of patient

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A CDTM patient is a person referred to a pharmacist by his supervising physician for the purpose of receiving collaborative drug therapy management services. The supervising physician shall assess the patient and include a diagnosis when referring. The patient shall be notified of, and shall consent to, the services in the retail drug business setting. INDIVIDUAL REFERRAL AND CONSENT SHALL BE RECORDED BY THE PHARMACIST AND THE SUPERVISING PHYSICIAN in the patient's record.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Medicine regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Referral means the individual patient referral by a supervising physician to an authorized pharmacist for the purpose of receiving CDTM services IN A COMMUNITY PHARMACY SETTING. IN ALL OTHER PRACTICE SETTINGS, Referral means the CONSULTATION of a supervising physician and an authorized pharmacist about a patient for that purpose. In the community pharmacy setting the supervising physician shall execute a written CDTM referral which shall include, but is not limited to, the patient's name and address, the primary diagnosis for which CDTM services are authorized, the diagnosis of any comorbid conditions for which they are authorized, any known patient drug allergies, a statement that the patient has executed a written consent, and any other specific instructions to the authorized pharmacist.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: A pharmacist may ISSUE, MODIFY OR DISCONTINUE a prescription or medication order AS AUTHORIZED IN a collaborative practice agreement meeting the requirements of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2. The power is three-fold and each of the three acts must be authorised by the agreement itself, so an agreement that authorises one does not by implication authorise the others.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: The first requirement in 105 CMR 700.003(G) is that the pharmacist MEETS ALL APPLICABLE REQUIREMENTS OF THE BOARD OF REGISTRATION IN PHARMACY established in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24, and 247 CMR 1.00 THROUGH 16.00. The condition is not confined to the collaborative practice regulation; it reaches every applicable Board requirement across that range.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: The pharmacist registers with the Department, in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004, and with the DEA IF APPLICABLE in accordance with 21 CFR 1300, FOR THE PURPOSE OF PRESCRIBING under 105 CMR 700.000. The purpose of the registration is part of the requirement, so a registration obtained for dispensing does not carry prescribing authority, and the federal limb bites only where it is applicable.
exceptions: The DEA limb applies only if applicable

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(3) the pharmacist issues, modifies or discontinues a prescription or medication order IN ACCORDANCE WITH M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, 105 CMR 700.000, 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12, AND THE COLLABORATIVE PRACTICE AGREEMENT between the pharmacist and supervising physician established in accordance with 247 CMR 16.00 and 243 CMR 2.12.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(4) the pharmacist, IF PRACTICING IN A RETAIL SETTING, may issue a prescription for a controlled substance IN SCHEDULE VI ONLY, in accordance with 105 CMR 700.003(G)(3).
exceptions: The subparagraph is addressed to a pharmacist practising in a retail setting; it states no ceiling for a pharmacist practising elsewhere.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: The pharmacist may dispense a controlled substance for immediate treatment in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 9, PROVIDED the pharmacist is authorized by 105 CMR 700.003(G) to prescribe that substance. The pharmacist may order from a drug wholesaler, manufacturer, laboratory or distributor, for purposes of dispensing for immediate treatment, those controlled substances IN SCHEDULE VI which the pharmacist is authorized to prescribe. For Schedules II through V dispensed for immediate treatment, the pharmacist may obtain such controlled substances ONLY as supplied by the supervising physician or obtained through a prescription or medication order for the patient.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(9) the pharmacist MAINTAINS A RECORD of any controlled substance maintained for the purpose of dispensing for immediate treatment or administering pursuant to 105 CMR 700.000 and any related Department guidelines.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: The pharmacist may issue a prescription in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20, PROVIDED that the prescribing pharmacist CLEARLY IDENTIFIES THEIR NAME AND PROFESSIONAL DESIGNATION to the dispensing pharmacist and provides their REGISTRATION NUMBER, WORK ADDRESS, PHONE NUMBER, AND THE NAME OF THE SUPERVISING PHYSICIAN.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: The pharmacist may prescribe a controlled substance for a patient IN A LICENSED HEALTH FACILITY, including a hospital, long term care facility, ambulatory care clinic or hospice, THROUGH THE USE OF A WRITTEN MEDICATION ORDER ENTERED ON THE PATIENT'S MEDICAL RECORD MAINTAINED AT THE FACILITY, provided that such a written order meets all applicable provisions of 105 CMR 700.000.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10) the pharmacist PROVIDES A COPY of an initial prescription OR a modification OR a discontinuation of a prescription TO THE SUPERVISING PHYSICIAN WITHIN 24 HOURS OF ITS ISSUANCE, UNLESS MORE URGENT NOTIFICATION IS REQUIRED UNDER THE CIRCUMSTANCES. The duty sits on the pharmacist, the period runs from issuance, and it reaches a modification or a discontinuation as well as an initial prescription.
exceptions: Where more urgent notification is required under the circumstances, the 24-hour period is not the standard; the proviso shortens the time rather than extending it.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

rule_dependencies.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f), if prescriptive practices are included in a collaborative practice agreement the pharmacist must maintain a current controlled substance registration issued by the Department during the term of the agreement pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, §§ 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000; complete the training required under M.G.L. c. 94C, § 18(e) before initially obtaining that controlled substance registration and at least biennially thereafter as a condition precedent to renewing the pharmacist licence; and submit an attestation, signed under the pains and penalties of perjury, that the pharmacist participates in, or has applied to participate in, MassHealth either as a provider of services or for the limited purpose of ordering and referring services covered by MassHealth.

findings.location: orientation[5].text, the sentence beginning "The implementing regulation, 247 CMR 16.04(7), states the same three propositions in the same order"
findings.problem: 247 CMR 16.04(7) does not state the three employment propositions in the statute's order. M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(e) runs: the permission for a physician or physician group to hire pharmacists; then the prohibition on a retail pharmacy employing a physician for the purpose of maintaining, establishing or entering into a collaborative practice agreement with a patient; then the saving for quality-assurance hiring. 247 CMR 16.04(7) runs: (a) the hiring permission; (b) "A community pharmacy may hire a physician or licensed medical practitioner to conduct quality assurance reviews of pharmacists engaged in collaborative drug therapy management"; and (c) "No community pharmacy may employ a physician for the purpose of maintaining, establishing or entering into a collaborative practice agreement". The second and third propositions are transposed, so the claim "in the same order" is contradicted by the regulation the sentence is describing.
findings.rationale: The section's whole pedagogy is close textual reading, and this sentence makes an express claim about the structure of a regulation that the regulation's own text refutes; that is a fidelity defect on its face rather than a stylistic preference. Severity is Low, not Medium, because the error is self-limiting: the same sentence, the comparison table "Employment: which direction of hiring is allowed, and for what purpose" and worked_examples[2].steps[3] all attach the correct subparagraph letters (16.04(7)(b) to the quality-assurance permission and 16.04(7)(c) to the prohibition), and the three propositions themselves are paraphrased accurately, including the correctly flagged retail pharmacy / community pharmacy vocabulary difference and the statute's closing words "with a patient". No Massachusetts fact pattern taught in this section, and none of the eleven mapped practice questions, is decided wrongly by the error; the repair is the deletion of three words.

results.summary: Checked every field of the section against M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, 247 CMR 16.00 and 243 CMR 2.12 read directly from the official sources on 2026-09-12. The substance is accurate throughout and unusually careful where the three instruments diverge. Verified as correct: the four core verbs and the three conditions on the laboratory limb, including the diagnostic boundary and the fact that the history and vital-signs limbs carry no condition; all six statutory qualification elements, including the conditional chapter 118E element; 247 CMR 16.02(1)(a) through (e) in the regulation's own words, including "current unrestricted license in good standing", "$1,000,000 (per occurrence) ... during the term ... which specifically covers drug therapy management", the five-contact-hour element with no continuing education unit alternative, and the closed doctor of pharmacy route in 16.02(1)(c)1. tied to an agreement entered on or before June 30, 2017; the three limbs of Authorized Pharmacist in 243 CMR 2.12(1); 243 CMR 2.12(2)(c) and (e) as the looser statements of the credential and continuing-education elements; the four settings in s. 24B1/2(c)(1) through (4) with their approving bodies, the shared c. 111, s. 51 licensing of hospitals and ambulatory care clinics, and the cumulative on-site supervision condition in the clinic limb; the employment rules in s. 24B1/2(e) and 247 CMR 16.04(7); 243 CMR 2.12(3)(a) through (e), including that a controlled substances registration event alone deems a physician ineligible and that notification under (3)(e) is discretionary and is not triggered by a registration event; the statutory Patient definition with its retail-setting notice and consent and its two-professional recording duty; and both meanings of Referral in 243 CMR 2.12(1) with its expressly non-exhaustive contents list, kept properly distinct from the physician's unqualified duty under 243 CMR 2.12(3)(c). All nineteen retrieval_prompts answers are legally correct. All eleven mapped practice questions (MA-Q-0081, 0301 through 0306, 0342, 0343, 0360 and 0416) are answerable from the section and none is contradicted by it. One defect: a single sentence in orientation[5] asserts that 247 CMR 16.04(7) states the three employment propositions in the statute's order, which it does not. That is a Low-severity fidelity slip with no effect on any answer, and the disposition is MINOR_EDIT rather than KEEP only because a KEEP would publish a sentence that is false about the regulation it cites.

results.summary: Checked every field against the current 105 CMR 700.000 (the 39-page edition served at /doc/105-cmr-700-implementation-of-mgl-c94c-0/download), 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) and M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20 on 2026-09-12, and found nothing wrong. The opening words of 105 CMR 700.003(G) are reproduced faithfully, including the conjunctive list of 247 CMR 16.00, 243 CMR 2.12 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2 and the closing proviso; reading "as authorized in" distributively across issue, modify and discontinue is the natural reading of the text and is reinforced by (G)(3). The paragraph carries exactly ten numbered requirements and the section states all ten accurately; its casting claim is verified against the text, since (1), (2), (3), (9) and (10) are written as duties (the pharmacist meets, registers, issues, maintains, provides) while (4) through (8) are written as permissions with provisos of their own. Verified individually: (1)'s range over the whole of 247 CMR 1.00 through 16.00; (2)'s "in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004", the purpose element "for the purpose of prescribing under 105 CMR 700.000" (which 105 CMR 700.004(A)(2) corroborates, pharmacists being required to register separately for each business or professional activity), and the conditional DEA limb referred out to 21 CFR 1300; (3)'s five conformity referents including the agreement; (4)'s Schedule VI ceiling fastened to a pharmacist "if practicing in a retail setting" and cross-referenced to (G)(3); (5)'s dependence on prescribing authority the pharmacist already has; (6)'s wholesaler route for Schedule VI and its closed supply route for Schedules II through V; (7)'s two clearly-identified and four provided particulars, with work address and phone number listed separately and the supervising physician's name among them, and M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20 correctly described as the general law's oral prescription provision; (8)'s written medication order entered on the patient's medical record maintained at the facility, with the four named facilities correctly treated as illustrative of "a licensed health facility" because the regulation introduces them with "including"; (9)'s record duty; and (10)'s 24 hours running from issuance, covering a modification and a discontinuation as well as an initial prescription, with a proviso that can only shorten the period. (10) is indeed the only clock in the paragraph. The three conditions in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)1. through 3. are stated accurately and each is correctly fastened (the registration to the term of the agreement, the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(e) training to renewal of the pharmacist licence, the MassHealth attestation to a sworn state of affairs), and the section keeps that registration properly distinct from the one required by 105 CMR 700.003(G)(2). All eight mapped practice questions (MA-Q-0292, 0333, 0334, 0337, 0338, 0339, 0353 and 0354) are answerable from the section and none is contradicted by it. The scope boundaries to the companion sections on the practice, the agreement and the retail regime are drawn honestly and no proposition reaches beyond them.
